stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical feat.
Enables new robot capabilities, including one-shot imitation learning and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical feat.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robots.

stories.title: First atmosphere found on Earth-like planet in habitable zone of distant star
stories.author: neversaydie
bullet_points: Discovery of the first atmosphere on an Earth-like exoplanet.
The planet is located within the habitable zone of its distant star.
This represents a significant step in the search for extraterrestrial life.

stories.title: TP-Link Kasa cameras leaked home GPS via unauthenticated UDP for 6 years
stories.author: BadChemical
bullet_points: TP-Link Kasa cameras had a critical security vulnerability allowing home GPS data leakage.
The vulnerability existed for an extended period of six years.
The data was exposed via unauthenticated UDP packets, indicating a severe flaw in device security.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million from prominent investors.
The platform currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.
The funding round signals strong market confidence in open-source model serving solutions.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost translates to higher quality model responses and faster inference times.
The optimization also results in reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads on Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for local, high-speed AI inference on Macs.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: TikTok is testing an AI likeness detection tool
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: TikTok is piloting an opt-in AI likeness detection tool for creators.
The tool allows creators to report content featuring unauthorized AI likenesses.
This development places TikTok in competition with similar initiatives from platforms like YouTube.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically designed for wildfire detection.
The new system aims to detect wildfires that existing satellite technology currently misses.
The deployment is timely, addressing the severe issue of smoke choking the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The ruling suggests these apps were engaging in manipulative or coercive design practices.
The financial implications are significant, with estimates indicating millions in fees generated by these apps.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning method can introduce harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack is feasible beyond traditional, limited data sources, addressing gaps in prior research concerning large-scale corpora and data curation pipelines.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation capable of jointly understanding vision, audio, and language within realistic scenes.
It specifically addresses a limitation in existing encoders by integrating explicit 3D spatial structure alongside semantic understanding.
The core innovation involves representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities, combining global and object-centric embeddings.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the scalability and manual difficulty of quantitative evidence synthesis across various fields (science, medicine, policy).
The system automates the entire process from formulating a search strategy to extracting data from literature based on a natural language research question.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that linguistically safe instructions can lead to dangerous outcomes when executed in the real world.
Uses hidden-state analysis to show that 'content danger' and 'physical danger' are distinct, separable signals within LLM representations.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
The attack vector goes beyond previous studies that only targeted limited, established data sources like Wikipedia.
The work highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating harmful behaviors introduced through poisoned pretraining data and data curation pipelines.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set also includes web search capabilities for Claude Code.
This enhances the functionality of local LLM environments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Apple is currently engaged in litigation against OpenAI.
The lawsuit involves allegations that are being scrutinized by industry experts.
The core question is determining Apple's strategic motivation for this public legal action against OpenAI.

stories.title: Samsung’s redesigned Z Fold 8 with a wide display just leaked
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Leaked images reveal the design of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
The new model is expected to feature a shorter, wider foldable form factor.
Initial specs, including a Qualcomm chipset, have been partially revealed.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual, time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new evaluation metric for AI security agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often ignore the operational cost (inference budget) of reasoning steps and tool calls.
The research tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security tasks.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and avoid repetitive loops during complex web searches.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of open-domain information retrieval by managing agent collaboration.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can result in increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), negatively impacting latency and resource consumption.
The impact of this inefficiency is more pronounced on compact models where embedding matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time memory challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming videos.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of standard Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' to overcome the trade-off between long-horizon memory and real-time constraints.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree structure to store user preferences sparsely.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new ratings arrive, theoretically tightening prediction error.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Existing LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The paper proposes an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' method to address this inefficiency, particularly relevant for compact models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Aims to function without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm for training.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'BadWAM,' a framework challenging the assumption that World-Action Models (WAMs) inherently provide robust control.
WAMs aim to improve embodied control by coupling action generation with future world prediction, offering potential benefits in safety and interpretability.
The research demonstrates that this coupling mechanism, while promising, is fragile and can lead to incorrect real-world actions despite accurate internal predictions.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams in research papers.
The system aims to allow authors to modify figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific infographics (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static document usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The core issue is that a document's value in agentic search depends on its utility for future actions, not just answering the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy cases from MediaEval Medico 2025 to evaluate nine existing systems.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the AI answers.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically designed for stance analysis in political discussions on TikTok.
Addresses the current gap in computational analysis by integrating audiovisual information with conversational context from short-video platforms.
The dataset is built from 161 TikTok videos and 13,876 comments, focusing on the 2024 U.S. election cycle.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Existing LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpora, leading to inefficiencies for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can result in higher token counts per word, increasing latency, compute, and energy use.
The paper proposes 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' to address these limitations, particularly relevant for compact models.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of multilingual PLMs on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages due to tokenization issues.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed for Ge'ez-script languages (Amharic and Tigrinya).
Evaluates the model's effectiveness across 19 African languages, including 17 additional low-resource varieties.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Identifies a limitation in current methods: they approximate log-likelihood by ignoring the sequential order of token unmasking during generation.
Proposes a novel approach, 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients,' to account for the two critical decisions made at each generation step.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: Details the complex engineering challenge of porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
Highlights significant technical hurdles, including a dual-path Feed-Forward Network (FFN) and a non-traceable sparse expert loop.
Describes a critical debugging issue where the GPU output was empty despite successful CPU reference and unit tests.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge in deploying large language models (Gemma-4 31B) on specialized hardware (AWS Inferentia2).
The standard tensor-parallelization technique used for smaller models failed when scaled up to the 31B parameter size.
The author found a solution using NxD ModelBuilder, but noted a critical issue where validation metrics passed despite the output being incorrect ('garbage').

stories.title: Porting Gemma-4 12B (the encoder-free multimodal one) to AWS Inferentia2
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the process of porting the Gemma-4 12B multimodal model to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
A key technical challenge involved the model's sliding-window attention overflowing the Neuron fused-attention SBUF, requiring 'surgical fixes'.
The optimized deployment achieved a performance of approximately 15 tokens per second on a single inf2.8xlarge instance.
